chapters.title: Already on a ship
pages: Put furnace fuel in the generator. Open the Ship Controller, choose a destination, then Engage. The Trip tab shows what happens next. You can walk around during FTL.
Signals are optional. Visit signal approaches and docks. Ignore it to keep travelling. Return to your ship and press Continue journey to depart; the jump is already paid.

chapters.title: Build my first ship
pages: Craft the basic parts, Pad Computer, Ship Controller, generator, engine and Air Supply. Their recipes follow in this order under Recipes.
Register a dirt or grass pad inside a cobblestone ring. Build the ship above it: a sealed cabin, framed exit, inward-facing Air Supply and outward-facing engine.
Leave headroom at the controller and clear exhaust behind the engine. Add fuel, open the controller and choose Launch. Follow any named repair instruction, then retry.

chapters.title: Landing pads
pages: Make a flat dirt/grass rectangle inside a complete cobblestone ring, at most 32 x 32. Put the Pad Computer on the ring and choose Register pad.
Show pad area marks what stays on the ground. Keep the ship within 32 blocks above the floor and leave clear sky. Registering a pad does not build a ship.

chapters.title: Ship beacons
pages: Put a Ship Beacon on a registered pad ring. Stand clear, choose a design, then Deliver ship. Keep the pad and sky empty. Delivery includes the existing ship design and supplies.
Wait until construction finishes. Enter the ship, check fuel and air, then use its controller. An interrupted delivery uses recovery; do not deliver another hull over it.

chapters.title: Hull and cargo
pages: Connect ship blocks through full faces. Use full blocks or glass for pressure walls. Stairs, slabs and panes are fittings. A framed door or hatch gives access.
Containers and their contents travel with the hull. Stop pistons and pending block actions before departure. Inspect names blocks that need repair or removal.

chapters.title: Controllers
pages: Ship Controller: choose a destination, Engage, fly manually or manage systems. Manual steps also offer Launch, Jump, Land, Dock and Undock.
Scanner: browse destinations and Set destination. This changes the shared selection; it never starts travel. Return to the Ship Controller to Engage.

chapters.title: Ship power
pages: Generators burn furnace fuel for electricity and propulsion. Batteries store electricity and cover shortages up to their discharge limit. A charged battery does not replace jump fuel.
Open each machine to check its switch, fuel or charge. Keep Controls, Air and Engines powered. Upgrade modules improve machinery; scarce fuel still needs a reserve for the return trip.

chapters.title: Spatial air
pages: Point an Air Supply into a room and leave its outlet clear. Air spreads between connected spaces. Open interior doors to refill other rooms; repair exterior leaks.
Room air and your oxygen are different readings. Low oxygen warns you to return to air. Healthy cabin air stays quiet. Use machine room readings to find a weak pump or leak.

chapters.title: Doors and groups
pages: Interior doors may stay open during travel. Close exterior doors and hatches to keep the cabin sealed. Engage closes exterior doors; Close all doors remains a manual command.
For docking, put a normal door over an outward-facing Docking Base. Frame the door, leave standing room behind it and a clear approach outside.

chapters.title: Suits and EVA
pages: Wear all four suit pieces before leaving a safe cabin. Armor alone is not an air source. Carry an Air Canister and use it on an Air Supply to refill it.
In space, the suit permits EVA flight within the 72-block tether. On an airless planet, gravity remains normal. Watch suit air and return before supplies run out.

chapters.title: Launch and land
pages: Close exterior openings and keep everyone inside breathable cabins. At the controller, choose a destination and Engage. Launch and landing move the real hull between dimensions.
A short transition waits for passengers and the destination view. Stay aboard until it finishes. Reconnecting follows the saved arrival; do not dismantle a ship during transfer.

chapters.title: Planet travel
pages: Every nongas planet and moon has its own surface. Ocean and jungle worlds have breathable air; other types need a suit and air. Terra is the Overworld.
Choose a landing pad on your destination planet and Engage. The first visit creates a starter pad. Lava can allow arrival but remains dangerous and can obstruct takeoff.

chapters.title: Scanners
pages: Open the Scanner. Browse Stars, a system, then a planet or berth. Highlight a result and Set destination. Go back to the Ship Controller and Engage.
Grey map targets need intermediate hops or better engines. Set a reachable next stop. Each hop is a separate trip. Sensor equipment needs Cameras power.

chapters.title: Star systems
pages: The Scanner map shows Sol, four other systems and features. Engine tiers reach 25/40/60/100 light-years. Hop through reachable places to go farther; keep fuel for returning.

chapters.title: Piloting
pages: Controller > Fly manually. W/S thrust, A/D yaw, Space/Ctrl lift. Up/Down pitch, Q/E roll. R brakes, F fires. H shows controls; Esc stops and returns to the controller.
Manual flight stays in the current region. To travel farther, choose another destination and Engage. Keep fuel and power aboard and avoid planets and other hulls.

chapters.title: Stations and docks
pages: Select a station berth and Engage. Wait for approach, capture and collar completion. Open the connected dock door and walk through to board.
Return through the same port. For an encounter, Continue journey handles departure. For ordinary docking, Undock from your visiting ship. Public stations cannot be claimed.
To build a station, carry a Station Core, suit and module kits. Deploy the core in space using its placement action. Build and connect rooms from the core controls.

chapters.title: Claim a salvage ship
pages: Board an unclaimed salvage vessel and open its Station Core. Choose Claim. A damaged core can be replaced with a Ship Controller; open it aboard the wreck to claim it.
Claiming keeps the same hull, cargo, fuel and damage. You receive its title. Your previous ship stays where you left it; claiming does not scrap or replace it.
Return through the connected port to use your original ship. To recover either owned ship later, use My ships at a surface Pad Computer. Keep both ships clear of crew before storage.

chapters.title: Store and deploy ships
pages: Stand beside a surface Pad Computer and open My ships. Choose your ship, then Store. Everyone must leave it first. Storage clears the pad and gives the owner a title.
To deploy, choose the stored ship at a clear pad and stay by the computer. A carried matching title is consumed after success; a refused deployment keeps it. Owners can replace a lost title.

chapters.title: Damage and cannon
pages: The cannon needs connected hardware and Weapons power. F fires while piloting. Damage breaks real hull blocks and can vent a cabin; repair leaks before travelling.

chapters.title: Cameras
pages: Place a Camera facing the view. Right-click to name and preview it. Mount Monitor tiles in a rectangle up to 8 x 8, then right-click a tile to choose a camera.
In fullscreen, arrows aim, Page Up/Down zoom, Tab changes feeds and Esc returns. A distant view does not run remote machines or explosives.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
pages: Cannot launch? Inspect the hull. Fix the named block, close exterior openings, clear exhaust and sky, and get crew inside safe cabins.
No power or air? Check generator fuel, machine switches and power allocation. Clear the Air Supply outlet. Open interior doors to distribute air; close exterior leaks.
Cannot land or dock? Check the current planet, selected pad/berth, occupancy and construction status. Finish the current maneuver before starting another.

chapters.title: Crafting notes
pages: Recipes follow basic parts, flight systems, suit supplies, upgrades and later equipment. Hover an ingredient for its name; click it to open its recipe. Mirroring works, rotation does not.

chapters.title: NullOS terminal
pages: Computer Terminal opens NullOS for files and ship scripts. Controls power enables ship calls. Up/Down recalls commands; Ctrl-C stops a job; Shift-Esc closes the terminal.

chapters.title: Shell commands
pages: Start with help, ls and ship status. Read a file with cat name.py. Run one with python name.py or bash name.sh. All paths remain inside the ship computer.
Use edit name.py, type lines, then a single . line or Ctrl-S to save. Ctrl-C cancels. Pipes and > / >> work for basic file processing.

chapters.title: Scripts and jobs
pages: Detached jobs: run --detach file.py, ps, kill ID. Files and jobs persist with the ship. These are limited Bash/Python-style languages; see help for supported calls.

chapters.title: Native ship API
pages: Try ship rooms, ship scan local and ship doors all close. Scripts obey the same power and crew safety checks as buttons. World actions wait while hull chunks are unloaded.
